findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the datetime ordering used by its only caller
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The audit-log endpoint enables this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime, not a number, and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor invokes get_item_key for results, so any authorized request with optimized_pagination=true fails with a 500 instead of returning a page. DateTimePaginator handles this by converting via strftime first; this class does not. Its value_from_cursor also returns the raw integer cursor value, while build_queryset for a datetime column needs the datetime conversion DateTimePaginator performs, so subsequent pages would filter incorrectly even if the key conversion were fixed.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing raises AssertionError on Django querysets
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset is negative, this passes a negative start (and possibly a negative stop when limit+extra is smaller than the offset magnitude) into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets explicitly do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. Since cursor offsets are parsed from the user-supplied cursor string, an authorized audit-log user can craft a negative-offset cursor and trigger an unhandled 500 rather than a BadPaginationError or a valid page. The same unguarded negative offset remains reachable for is_prev cursors in BasePaginator.get_result at line 182.

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None for superusers without org membership
findings.body: The new gate dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally whenever the optimized path is evaluated (for every request, since enable_advanced is computed before the branch). For a superuser accessing an organization they are not a member of, member can be None, so this raises AttributeError and breaks the previously working audit-log endpoint for exactly the superuser case the check tries to allow (the 'or' short-circuit only helps when is_superuser is already true; a non-superuser request still evaluates member, and contexts where member is None for other reasons crash as well). The member access needs a None guard.

findings.title: Switching span sets from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight segments with WRONGTYPE errors
findings.body: This changes the on-Redis type of span-buf:s:* keys from a Redis SET (sadd/sscan/scard/sunionstore) to a ZSET (zadd/zscan/zcard/zunionstore in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua) with no key versioning, draining, or dual-type handling. During a rolling deploy, keys created by old consumers are SETs; new code calling ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN on them returns WRONGTYPE, failing process_spans/flush for those traces, and old consumers similarly fail on new ZSET keys during rollback. Buffered keys live up to redis_ttl (3600s), so in-flight segments will error and can be dropped for up to an hour around deploys.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction can silently drop the segment/root span and leaves has_root_span stale
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin evicts the lowest-scored (earliest end_timestamp_precise) members with no metric or log, silently discarding real span payloads rather than flagging the oversized segment as the previous flush-time check did. The evicted members can include the segment/root span (e.g. a short root span, clock skew, or a root whose children report later precise end times); the has_root_span flag computed just below still returns true because it is based on the stored flag or is_root_span of the current insert, so the now root-less segment is queued with the short root timeout and flushed as an incomplete segment. Buffer.py also removed the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data (line 449), so there is no longer any flush-side detection of oversized segments produced by pre-change keys or any path that bypasses this eviction.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction, score-ordering, or paginator behavior
findings.body: The test changes only add the now-required end_timestamp_precise field to existing Span constructions. Nothing exercises a segment growing past 1000 spans to verify zpopmin eviction keeps the intended (latest/root) spans, nothing verifies segments are ordered or deduplicated correctly after the SET-to-ZSET migration, and there are no tests at all for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized_pagination branch in the audit-log endpoint, which currently crash on datetime keys and negative offsets. The core behavioral change of this PR is therefore unverified.
